question: During the British rule in India, when did transfer of capital from Calcutta to Delhi take place?
solution:
The Correct answer is **'1911'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Year 1911, Delhi became the Capital of British India, and it was shifted from **Calcutta to Delhi**. 
 
• The decision was taken during the Reign of Lord Harding, who was the Viceroy of India. 
 
• Hoarding said that Calcutta was located in** Extreme east of India** so capital of India should be centralized in the terms of geographically for betterment.
 
• Some historians stated that the situation in Bengal was gradually going out of control & rigorous and extremist movement was giving sleepiness nights to the British India.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The foundation stone was laid by **King George V and Queen Marry** at the site of Delhi Durbar, Kingsway Camp on 15th December 1911.​​​
 
• Approximately 89 years were spent by the British as the **dominant force **in India.
 
• The British established their hegemony, commonly known as colonialism, in India after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.
 
• The** British East India Company **ruled India prior to the British throne.
